why: Test log: 'dd: error writing /mnt/lustre/f907a.sanity: No such process' on repeat 2 after the injected OBD_FAIL_OST_EROFS write error reached dd. PS1 only renamed test_907 to 907a with the same dd write; the identical 'dd failed' is the known fleet-wide failure LU-19997 (sanity test_907: dd failed, opened 2026-03-16, 100 failures over 37+ changes), so the rename hid it from history matching. The patch's later PS3 commit message describes exactly this pre-existing test flaw and rewrites the test.

bugs.reason: single unit, 4 failures, all the same dd ESRCH on the second iteration: the ambient LU-19997 test flaw (multiple writes let the failed write RPC land before unlink), not the patch's mdc change.

notes: Renamed tests lose their failure history: a 'patch-changes-test' label on a renamed test should be checked against the old name's history (test_907 here, ticket LU-19997) before calling it the patch's. Subtest-change sessions repeat the test (ONLY_REPEAT), which raises the hit rate of an existing flaky test and makes it look patch-specific. Later patchsets (2, 3) fail differently ('multiop failed' in 907a and 907b on many groups): that is a genuine new patch bug, separate from this one.

why: test_165 is new in this patch (later renumbered 167) and greps dmesg for the patch's new CWARN 'osd-ldiskfs: retry loading module'. All 4 failures (el9.7 and three el10 custom runs) fail at exactly repeat 11 of ONLY_REPEAT=40 with 'loading osd-ldiskfs was not retried' and no retry line in dmesg, consistent with console rate limiting of the repeated message; later patchsets read the debug log with lctl dk instead and stop failing this way.

bugs.reason: one bug: the new test depends on a console message that is rate limited after about ten repeats; deterministic at iteration 11 on every distro.

notes: Clean case: test added by the patch, never seen elsewhere, deterministic. The deterministic repeat number across sessions is itself a strong signal that the fault is in the test design (rate limit), not a flake.

why: Every new sanity-ec test_8a..8j fails at the patch's own lfs mirror extend --ec: 'lfs mirror mirror: cannot get UNLOCK lease, ext 24 ... Operation not supported (95)' then 'cannot merge layout'. The patch adds the stale merge (LL_LEASE_ALLOW_STALE) that needs OBD_CONNECT2_FLR_EC and changes test-framework module options to enable it; on PS19 the feature was not negotiated, in every session (subtest-change, zfs part-7, custom). Tests are new to the patch, never failed elsewhere, and later patchsets (20+) do not fail them.

bugs.reason: one bug: all nine units (six different signatures) fail on the same EOPNOTSUPP from the lease merge (FLR_EC connect flag or MDT tunable not enabled by the patch's test-framework/module option change), checked in 8a, 8e, 8h, 8i logs.

notes: Error signatures here are the test's own error() text, which differs per subtest and per lfs mode, while the underlying failure line (lease ext 24 EOPNOTSUPP) is identical. Grouping by sig would give 6 bugs for 1. A grouping rule that keys on the first error line of the tool output (or on the shared root cause in the log) would collapse these correctly.

why: Test-only patch adding sanity-ec 35a-c and 60a-i, which grep 'Wrote parity #N range=...' from lfs mirror resync against hard-coded ranges. The sampled 60a fails 'Did not find the first expected block' (inside a piped while loop, so the recorded sig is the run_one fallback 'test_60a failed with 1'). The tests are new, never fail elsewhere, and failed the same way on PS44 to 46: the patch's expectations do not match the parity coverage the code produces.

bugs.reason: ldiskfs (review-dne-subtest-change and the ldiskfs custom run): only 60a and 60b fail, with 'Did not find the first expected block' (range mismatch at the start of a stripe; 60c, 60d and 60e pass on ldiskfs).

ZFS (zfs subtest-change and the fstype=zfs custom run): 60b reports 'Wrong number of blocks written. 4 but expected 2', a different failure from ldiskfs; SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE granularity on ZFS differs so every hard-coded range is wrong. 60e/f/h ('Did not find the expected block') fail only on ZFS and belong here.

notes: Same unit, same sig ('test_Nb failed with N') hides two distinct failures split by backend fs: the sig is the generic run_one fallback because error() ran inside a pipeline subshell, so the real first error line ('Wrong number of blocks' vs 'Did not find the first expected block') must be taken from the test log. Grouping should key on the first FAIL line, and on fstype when a test fails on only one backend. Arguably the ldiskfs and ZFS problems could be one 'test expectations wrong' bug, but they need different fixes.

why: conf-sanity test_157c is the patch's new 'timeout window coverage' test; the log shows 'Started fs1235-OST0001' and then 'FAIL: New OST1 should not register after timeout expired', i.e. the patch's allow_register timer (or the test-framework window it opens around target format, or the 24h auto-arm) left registration open. It fails on ldiskfs and ZFS, in part-3 and subtest-change, on 14 patchsets from PS2 to PS39, and never on any other change.

bugs.reason: one bug: the same assertion in every session and patchset.

notes: Rainshadow's verdict on these failures is 'covered' because they were linked to LU-18857, which is this patch's own ticket (open_changes lists 63425). A link to a ticket whose open change is the change under test should not turn a patch fault into 'covered'/ambient. The dataset's kind is right here, but the per-failure verdict would mislead a reader.

why: After the patch's gssiam_setup sets cli2mdt/cli2ost=gssiam, 'Mount with user_principal=mock_gssiam_deny' and the following remount give 'mount.lustre: mount ... at /mnt/lustre failed: Operation not permitted' with 'found 0/8 gssiam connections'. The tests (sanity-sec 103 to 106), the mock principal handling in l_gssiam_auth/tgt_gssiam and the fail_loc gating are all the patch's; nobody else fails these tests.

bugs.reason: sig 'mount failed': the same EPERM on the GSSIAM mock principal mount in all three tests (logs of 104, 105, 106 on part-2 and subtest-change), ldiskfs and ZFS.

sig 'flavor cliNmdt not gssiam before remount': only in review-dne-selinux-ssk-part-2; under GSS_SK the flavor counting helpers count SK contexts, so wait_flavor gssiam never succeeds. Distinct from the EPERM bug; the patch later excludes gssiam in flvr_cnt_* to fix it.

sig 'RW access failed' on review-ldiskfs-ubuntu only: 'touch: setting times of /mnt/lustre/test_rw_fset: Operation not permitted' after a successful gssiam mount; an Ubuntu-specific access bug that persists to PS87 (301 to 310 on Ubuntu).

'too large timeout' and 'mgc lock leak (4 != 5)' (the latter on the SSK group): one extra MGC lock per mount. Fails on this change and its series parent 64954 only (plus one other change), from 2026-03-30 to 2026-07-12; caused by the series, not by this test-only patch's diff.

notes: Three different bugs share the units sanity-sec 104/105/106; they split cleanly by signature and by test group (SSK, Ubuntu). The sanity test_901 units are a series bug (parent 64954) that rides along on every patchset of this change; a series-level grouping would avoid counting it once per change.

why: Ubuntu log: 'Starting client onyx-157vm120: -o /mnt/lustre ... onyx-157vm121' then 'mount.lustre: mount ... at /usr/lib/lustre/tests/onyx-157vm121 failed: Invalid argument': the patch's new test passes the client list and mount options to the mount helper in the wrong positions, so the second client's hostname becomes the mount point. Same in 104 and 105 on every group; only this change fails these tests.

bugs.reason: sig 'mount failed': argument misuse in the test's remount (hostname used as mount point), same line in every log; the PS7 'mount: bad usage' bug in a new form.
sig 'flavor cliNmdt not gssiam before remount': SSK group only, the GSS_SK flavor counting bug (same as PS24).
both sigs: series bug (extra MGC lock), as on PS7 and PS24.
Ubuntu session timed out (455 minutes) in sanity-sec cleanup after the failed remounts; most likely a consequence of the mount bug leaving clients unmounted, not checked in detail.

notes: How the bug evolves across 64955: PS7 'mount: bad usage' (args misordered), PS10 'Invalid argument' at a hostname mount point (still misordered), PS24 EPERM on the gssiam mount (args fixed, a real auth problem), PS87 the sanity-sec tests mostly pass except Ubuntu and a ZFS squash case, but the GSSIAM recovery tests now break the second client and cascade into sanityn and replay-ost-single. The signature 'mount failed' stays the same from PS7 to PS24 while the root cause changes three times, so a per-change bug identity keyed on (test, sig) across patchsets would merge different bugs.

why: Log: 'Starting client ...: user_xattr,flock,user_principal=mock_iam_rw -o /mnt/lustre ... trevis-156vm108' then 'mount: bad usage' and 'FAIL: mount failed'; the patch's test hands a space separated client list and options to the mount helper in the wrong order (also 'trevis-156vm108: command not found' from do_node). Test 104 is the patch's own (IAM flavor RW/RO) and fails only here.

bugs.reason: same 'mount: bad usage' line in both; test_103 comes from the series (it also fails on 64954 and 13 other changes of the same uploader's GSSIAM series in April), so one bug pattern shared across the series.
'too large timeout' and 'mgc lock leak (4 != 5)' (SSK): one extra MGC lock per mount from the series parent 64954.
'Autotest time out' in review-dne-subtest-change at repeat 28 with repeated 'already mounted' messages: a hang under ONLY_REPEAT, probably distinct from the bad usage bug; not checked further.

notes: sanity-sec test_103 is labelled patch-suspect with other_changes=8 and series_changes=3 but other_uploaders=0: the uploader has a 15-change GSSIAM series (64314 to 64321, 64954, 65061 to 65064, 65328, 65414) and test_103 at that time was a series test (master's test_103 is now an unrelated SSK test). 'Only this uploader' is correct here because the series is the cause, but test numbers are reused: master later used 103 to 106 for SSK tests, so history by test name alone mixes unrelated tests over time.

why: In review-dne-part-5 every sanityn NRS test 77a..77kg fails because the second client node cannot write ('dd: error writing ...: Input/output error' on onyx-158vm58) and 39a-c fail with 'Cannot send after transport endpoint shutdown' on the same node: the second client was left evicted or unusable before sanityn, after the patch's new GSSIAM recovery-small 180a-e tests (gssiam_setup unmounts and remounts other clients). The identical cascade hits review-dne-zfs-part-5 on PS87 and both part-5 sessions on PS88, never other changes, and is gone by PS96.

bugs.reason: one cascade: second client broken (EIO, ESHUTDOWN) after the GSSIAM recovery-small tests in part-5; 77ja 'touch failed' and 77jb 'failed to set tbf uid policy' are the same broken client, different symptoms. 77a and 77b (labelled unmatched) belong here too.

review-zfs: 'import is not in (FULL|IDLE) state' because the second client (trevis-152vm151) never returns to FULL; the session also fails insanity test_0 and replay-ost-single 2, 3, 7 (labelled ambient or unmatched). Most likely the same 'GSSIAM test leaves the other client broken' bug via the patch's replay-single 204/205; counted separately as it is a different suite and not proven.
review-ldiskfs-ubuntu only: RW, RO and squash checks all fail on Ubuntu (the PS24 Ubuntu 'RW access failed' bug persisting).

review-dne-zfs-part-2 el10.1: 'test_no_squash should be owned by root, got 65534' and 'stacked mount failed', persisting to PS96 on ldiskfs part-2 too; a squash/stacked mount bug distinct from the Ubuntu one in the same units.
'touch failed on writable mount' in zfs subtest-change (repeat run); possibly the squash bug, kept separate.
subtest-change: 'mcreate should fail for ro after eviction' (with 180a 'mkdir should fail for ro before failover'): RO principal not enforced around failover; the patch's own recovery tests.
SSK selinux group only; fails on 10 other changes (6 of the series) of the same uploader, so a series problem, cause not checked.

notes: Labels split one session's cascade across verdicts: sanityn 77a/77b are 'unmatched' (they have 2 branch failures) and 77k 'covered', while the rest of the same cascade is 'patch-suspect'; in review-zfs replay-ost-single 2, 3, 7 are 'ambient-no-ticket' and the rest 'patch-suspect'. Labelling and grouping should treat all failures after the first broken-client symptom in a session as one unit, and judge it once. The sampled test (77j) is not touched by the patch at all: the suspect label is right only because of a cascade from a different suite run earlier in the same session.
